25 years ago, evil attacked our nation, but it did not break the American spirit.

Today, we remember every innocent life taken on September 11, 2001, honor the extraordinary courage of our first responders, and remain forever grateful to the brave Americans who stepped forward to defend our uniquely American freedoms. 

We will always remember the strength our great nation showed in the face of unimaginable tragedy.
posts.summary: Honors 9/11 victims and first responders, affirms resilience

It’s hard to believe that a year ago today, Charlie Kirk’s life was tragically cut short by an act of leftwing political violence. His legacy, one of faith, courage, and passion for engaging the next generation, left a profound mark on our country while he was alive and has only grown stronger these past 12 months.

Wesley and I continue to pray for Erika, their precious children, and all who loved Charlie. His commitment to our country will never be forgotten.

In the wake of the September 11 attacks, Alabamian Johnny Micheal “Mike” Spann answered our nation’s call, deploying to Afghanistan as a CIA officer.

On November 25, 2001, he became the first American killed in combat in Afghanistan. Mike represented the very best of Alabama and America and we will never forget his and so many other courageous Americans’ service and sacrifice to our nation. https://t.co/ooZX8lLu0L

posts.text:
I’ll never forget sitting in class at the University of Alabama as we learned about the September 11 attacks.

The uncertainty and vulnerability we felt that morning will always stay with me, but so will the pride I felt watching brave men and women in uniform and heroic civilians run toward danger to help others in harm’s way.
